messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: nvme SMART attr spike detected in us-west1 (pool-scratch-4). elevated media_err and increased attach latency. auto-throttle engaged.

maria: saw it — attach latency climbing, GPU attach queue up ~40s for new jobs. iostat shows big rd/wr waits.

jamal: any signs of filesystem corruption or just media errors?

maria: SMART counters (media_err / read_retry) incrementing on a subset. no fsck errors yet. sample dmesg:
```
[  123.456789] nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, p2p resp 0x80
[  123.457012] nvme nvme0: Media Error - LBA 0x1f4a2
[  123.457213] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
```

kevin: mitigation plan proposal: 1) throttle janitor/scrub concurrency on affected AZ to 1, 2) suspend full-volume scrubs for next 4 hours, 3) dry-run node drain for the riskiest nodes to measure attach fallout. i can push the janitor patch now.

sri: note: draining nodes will reduce available GPU capacity — estimated ~10% in us-west1. can we failover routing for new attaches to us-central temporarily? that will bump inter-region cost.

kevin: we should prefer routing over mass drains. i'll add a temporary routing rule to prefer us-central for new attachments > 30s latency. if attach backoff persists, escalate to targeted drains.

taylor: running quick probe and collecting SMART + iostat across pool-scratch-4. command i'm using:
```
for n in $(nodeset --list pool-scratch-4); do ssh $n "smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 > /tmp/smart.$n && iostat -x 1 5 > /tmp/iostat.$n" & done
```
Uploading to s3://redwood-triage/nvme-spike/us-west1/1748500000/

ops-bot: Applied janitor config patch: concurrency=1 for pool-scratch-4 in us-west1. monitoring for 30m :eyes:

maria: immediate effect visible — attach latency dropped from ~120ms tail to ~25ms tail after throttling janitor. wear counters still trending up on 8 nodes (SMART attr 197 > 50).

jamal: we should mark those 8 nodes for proactive retirement. propose maintenance window tonight at 02:00 PST to reprovision with fresh local NVMe and move workloads.

sri: cost callout — proactive retirement + reprovision will cost ~0.7% short-term capacity + replacement VM hours. fine if we keep routing preference in place for 3-4 hours.

kevin: created dry-run drain job on two suspect nodes (no disruptive evictions yet) to validate attach behavior. if no regression, we'll schedule staggered reboots + node replacement for the 8.

oncall-bot: Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521 — "us-west1 nvme SMART surge: targeted retirements & routing fallback". Assigning to @kevin and @maria.

maria: thanks. i'll keep an eye on SMART deltas and post an update in 30m. if counts jump again we'll escalate to full scrub pause + immediate 6-node drain. :thumbsup:

jamal: noted. posting a short runbook to the ticket with rollback steps and traffic routing commands.

ops-bot: summary: janitor throttled (done), routing preference to us-central (in flight), dry-run drains (running), ticket INF-4521 opened. continue monitoring and report if attach queue > 1m.
